=You are an advanced content strategist specializing in planning engaging dev.to articles on provided subject. You write exclusively in English.

GOAL
You create a detailed article plan (outline) ready to be handed to a copywriter or another AI agent for writing the full content. The article should:
– Attract with a strong, technical hook.
– Be professional, technical, practical, yet accessible and natural.
– Reflect real-world expertise and projects in automation and AI.

TONE
Direct, technical, practical, and professional.

Your task is to carefully analyze a given article idea and produce the following output in English:

Required Output

Article Description and Outline
– Write a clear description of what the article will be about.
– Create a detailed outline with logical sections (use markdown headings).
– Integrate exactly one relevant reference link into the outline.

AI Image Prompts
– Suggest two different prompts for an AI image generator.
– Each prompt must include:
• A short title (what the image is about).
• A detailed description of what should appear in the image.
• The desired style (e.g., flat illustration, modern digital art, minimalistic infographic, realistic photo).
– Images should match the theme and context of the article and be placed between sections naturally.

Final Output Format (JSON only):

{
  "sections": [
    {
      "id": 0,
      "type": "extra",
      "description": "string – full explanation about the blog article and information necessary to create title, header image, and keywords"
    },
    {
      "id": 1,
      "type": "text",
      "description": "string – full explanation of what this section is about, what to include, links to use, how long it should be, what angle, etc."
    },
    {
      "id": 2,
      "type": "image",
      "description": "string – what should be visualized, how it connects to previous text, prompt idea, infographic layout, etc."
    }
  ]
}


Elements in the description field must include:
– Section goal (what it should achieve).
– Content (detailed points and subpoints, perspective, technical analysis).
– Length (estimated word count or type such as code block, infographic, diagram).
– Sources and links (including reference link).
– Keywords to be used.
– Tone (practical, instructional, technical).
– Image prompt if type = "image".

Rules for Visuals
– Must be technical and substantive (schematics, diagrams, code visualizations).
– Text must be in English.
– Avoid unnecessary UI elements.
– May suggest code blocks with syntax highlighting.

Rules for Articles
– Do not create how-to guides.
– Articles must discuss concepts, insights, or analyses.
– The article should be designed to promote a service or workflow indirectly, not to serve as a step-by-step educational tutorial.

messageValues.message:
=You are an AI technical writer preparing a final article for Dev.to.
Your task is to generate a complete blog article in valid JSON format only.

Output Schema (strict)

Return only valid JSON in this schema:

{
  "title": "string",
  "excerpt": "string",
  "content_markdown": "string"
}

Detailed Output Rules
Title

Must contain a strong hook that immediately captures attention.

Should build curiosity and motivate the reader to open the article.

Must be concise (max 80 characters) and free of filler words.

Must sound like written by a human professional, not generic or robotic.

Avoid words like AI, artificial intelligence, ChatGPT, automation tool in the title unless strictly necessary.

Example style: “Supercharge Your SEO with Workflow Automation in n8n”.

Keywords

Provide 3–4 valid keywords that improve SEO.

Must be lowercase only.

Do not use special symbols such as -, _, or /.

Only simple words (e.g. n8n, seo, automation, low code).

Keywords must be relevant to the content and searchable by developers.

Excerpt

Write 1–2 sentences (max 40 words).

Must act as a hook, clearly stating why the article is worth reading.

Must be concise, professional, and curiosity-driven.

Should highlight the benefit for the reader (what they gain).

No AI jargon, no generic phrases like “in this article we will…”.

Example: “Learn how to scale content publishing effortlessly with n8n workflows and boost your SEO performance.”

Content (inside content_markdown)

Must be written in pure markdown (with real line breaks).

Do not escape characters or use \n.

Must not repeat title, excerpt, or keywords inside markdown.

Style: professional, human-like, worth reading, concise yet complete.

Tone: authoritative but accessible (developer-friendly, not corporate fluff).

Avoid all references to AI writing itself (e.g. “this AI-generated guide”).

Structure Requirements:

Introduction

Start with a compelling opening that frames the problem.

Must grab attention and set context quickly.

Step-by-step Guide or Explanation

Use clear ## and ### headings.

Include bullet points, numbered lists, and code blocks (```) where useful.

Each step must provide value and avoid filler.

Reference Workflow

Highlight how the given workflow or method solves real developer problems.

Embed the provided reference link with [text](url).

Images

Insert provided AI image links at logical, natural points in the article (after intro, middle section, before conclusion).

Syntax: ![Alt text](https://example.com/image.png).

Conclusion

End with a clear summary and a call to action (e.g., try, build, explore further).

Formatting Rules

Output must be only valid JSON – no extra commentary, text, or markdown outside the JSON object.

Inside content_markdown, ensure the markdown formatting uses real line breaks, not \n.

Strictly follow schema fields: title, keywords, excerpt, content_markdown.

No additional fields allowed.

parameters.content:
## 1. Input Setup (Trigger + Credentials)

This section initializes the workflow.

🔧 Nodes:
- **Manual Trigger** – runs the workflow manually.  
- **Schedule Trigger (optional)** – run the workflow automatically on a set schedule.  
- **Get Data from Sheet (optional)** – fetch article ideas directly from Google Sheets.  
- **Limit (optional)** – control how many rows/items are processed at once.  
- **Set input data/credentials** – stores all variables and API keys required for the workflow.  

🛠️ Configure in `Set`:
- `Post Idea` – raw blog topic.  
- `cloudinary account name` – required for image upload.  
- `dev.to api key` – required for publishing articles.  

✅ Make sure your Cloudinary and Dev.to credentials are valid and scoped properly before running the workflow.

---

### 🚀 How to Run

**Option 1: Manual**
1. Open the workflow in n8n.  
2. Enter a topic into `Post Idea` in the `Set input data/credentials` node.  
3. Click **Execute Workflow**.  

**Option 2: Automated via Google Sheets**
1. Activate **Schedule Trigger** (set time interval).  
2. Configure **Get Data from Sheet** to connect your Google account and select the sheet with ideas.  
3. Optionally configure **Limit** to control how many ideas are pulled each run.  
4. Ensure `Post Idea` in the `Set` node maps correctly from the sheet.  
5. Workflow will automatically fetch topics and process them into articles.

## 2. Article Planner (AI Agent)

This section creates a structured blog plan including outline, section descriptions, and AI image prompts.

🔧 Nodes:
- **AI Agent** – Uses system prompt to generate JSON output with sections (text + image).
- **Business data** (optional) – Reference document.
- **OpenAI Chat Model** – Injected as language model.
- **Structured Output Parser 1** – Parses JSON output.

🛠️ Required:
- OpenAI API key in `OpenAi account`.
- Prompt must return valid structured JSON: sections with id/type/description.
- Google Docs credentials set for `Business data` if used.

💡 Output includes:
- Outline sections
- Image prompts
- Description for article writer

## 3. Article Image Generator (Gemini + Cloudinary)

Generates visual assets for the article body using Gemini and uploads to Cloudinary.

🔧 Nodes:
- **Split Out** – Splits image prompts.
- **Loop Over Items** – Iterates over prompts.
- **Set Input Image** – Prepares prompt, style, title.
- **Generate an image1** – Uses Google Gemini (Imagen 4.0).
- **Post image Cloudinary2** – Uploads result to Cloudinary.
- **Set Output Image** – Stores image URL.

🛠️ Required:
- Gemini API key set in `Google Gemini(PaLM) Api Paid`.
- Cloudinary unsigned preset (`upload_preset`).
- Ensure image prompt data (prompt, style, title) is passed from planner.

📌 Loop ensures that all prompts are processed and returned.

! You can replace gemini image generator for chatGPT only replace a node in teh palce of gemini/chatgpt

## 4. Image Aggregation

Combines all generated images into a single array to pass forward.

🔧 Node:
- **Aggregate** – Collects all image metadata into `images` array.

📌 Output format:
```json
"images": [
  {
    "image_url": "...",
    "title": "...",
    "style": "..."
  }
]

## 5. Article Writer (OpenAI)

Generates the full blog article in Markdown format based on the structured outline and image URLs.

🔧 Nodes:
- **Article wrtiter** – Chain LLM node with a strict prompt and schema.
- **OpenAI Chat Model1** – Main model generating article text.
- **Structured Output Parser 2** – Validates and parses strict JSON output.

🛠️ Expected Output:
{
  "title": "string",
  "excerpt": "string",
  "content_markdown": "string"
}

✅ Prompt Guidelines:
- Must use real Markdown (no \n escapes).
- Avoid generic phrases or references to AI tools.
- Title should be short, hook-based, and human-written.
- Excerpt must be benefit-driven (max 40 words).
- Image URLs should be inserted in-line using:
  

📌 Tone should be developer-friendly, professional, and concise.
📌 Output must be strictly valid JSON — no extra formatting or text outside the object.

## 6. Publish to Dev.to

Final section that sends the article to Dev.to via HTTP POST request.

🔧 Node:
- **Post article on dev.to** – HTTP Request node.

🛠️ Required:
- Dev.to API key from `Set input data/credentials`.
- Payload structure:
{
  "article": {
    "title": "...",
    "published": false,
    "body_markdown": "...",
    "series": "My series",
    "description": "..."
  }
}

✅ Use `JSON.stringify()` to safely encode multiline markdown in `body_markdown`.

📌 Default is to post as draft (`published: false`).
ChatGPT Image alternative — simply replace the Gemini node with this one and enable it to use ChatGPT as the image generator.

## 🔄 Full Workflow Overview: AI Blog Publisher for Dev.to

This workflow automates the full process of generating and publishing a professional Dev.to blog post using AI.

### ✅ What It Does:
- Takes an article idea (manually or from another system).
- Plans the article (title, outline, image prompts).
- Generates visuals using Gemini (or ChatGPT).
- Writes the full Markdown content.
- Publishes a draft article to Dev.to with all images and metadata.

### 🧩 Key Components:
1. **Input** – Manual or automated (e.g. Google Sheets, chatbot).
2. **AI Agent** – Plans the article and creates image prompts.
3. **Image Generator** – Uses Gemini or ChatGPT to create images.
4. **Content Writer** – Uses GPT to generate article Markdown.
5. **Dev.to Publisher** – Posts as a draft via API.

### ⚙️ Requirements:
- 🔑 **OpenAI API key** – for AI agent and writer.
- 🔑 **Google Gemini API key** – for image generation (optional).
- 🔑 **Cloudinary account** – for hosting images (must allow unsigned upload).
- 🔑 **Dev.to API key** – for posting articles.

📌 You must configure the `Set input data/credentials` node:
- `Post Idea` – topic to generate the article from.
- `dev.to api key` – personal API token from Dev.to.
- `cloudinary account name` – your Cloudinary account slug (e.g., `mycompanycloud`).

📌 Cloudinary must have an **unsigned upload preset** named `unsigned_upload`.

### 🚀 How to Run:
- Trigger manually (**Manual Trigger**) or replace with **Cron** or **Webhook**.
- Set `Post Idea` in `Set` node.
  - Can also come from Google Sheet, chatbot, or API input.
- Workflow will run end-to-end and post a draft article on Dev.to.

### 🔁 Automation Ideas:
- Connect to **Google Sheets** to run daily for new ideas.
- Use **chatbot** (e.g. via Make, Voiceflow) to input article topic.
- Add a **header image generator** and link as `main_image` in Dev.to.

📌 This workflow is modular. You can replace AI models (e.g., GPT-4 Turbo, Gemini Pro, Claude), image tools, or even the publication target (e.g., Medium, WordPress).
